question: For oil shale kerogen, why were the apparent activation energies obtained under air higher than those under nitrogen?
expect: premise false: under air they were LOWER over much of the conversion range (sec. 3.2); the paper also cautions they are not comparable intrinsic barriers
rendered:
Document "A Study on Pyrolysis Characteristics and Product Release Mechanisms of Oil Shale" is the most relevant to this question.

The apparent activation energies obtained under air were not higher than those under nitrogen. In fact, the apparent activation-energy values obtained under air were lower than those obtained under nitrogen over much of the investigated conversion range (page 4).
